text:
Alex: quick sketch: introduce a lightweight "hotkey shepherd" token to reduce eviction thrash for a tiny set of ultra-hot prefixes
Maria: shepherd token meaning? what's the invariant we aim to protect?
Alex: goal: avoid scatter reads and repeated rehydration. token is ephemeral, cooperative, and biases eviction & placement without replacing leases
Sam: so like a soft-pin but richer. what does it encode?
Alex: token = {level, epoch, last-write-hash}. level (0..3) controls grace window and replication of cached slices. epoch lets readers detect writers
Kevin: main correctness concern: cooperative tokens don't prevent concurrent demote+write races or stale tombstone exposure
Maria: agree. need clear rules for when writers must force hard invalidation vs when token remains optimistic
Sam: implementation idea: readers check epoch; if match, serve locally. writers bump epoch in coordination layer and emit an async invalidate hook. heavy invalidation only if hash mismatch or tombstone range touched
Alex: local config I tested quickly:
```
hotkey_shepherd:
  token_ttl_ms: 2500
  refresh_backoff_ms: 200
  levels:
    - name: warm
      grace_ms: 500
    - name: hot
      grace_ms: 2000
    - name: blazing
      grace_ms: 8000
```
Maria: fallback story? if node holding cache dies, other nodes must not violate write ordering when serving stale data
Kevin: we must treat shepherd token as optimization only. canonical path stays leases + tombstone propagation. tokens accelerate reads but must be invalidated on any write touching the segment
Sam: practical store: keep shepherd map in RAM on each prefix node. writers synchronously bump epoch in the central coord (fast path) but don't block reads except when epoch mismatches. Invalidation messages are best-effort but we record last-write-hash to detect divergence
Alex: telemetry we should add: token_hit_rate, token_invalidation_rate, post_invalidation_staleness_samples, evict_churn_per_shepherd_key
Maria: also read_latency_quantiles when token present vs absent, and token_memory_overhead per slab
Kevin: testing plan: unit tests for epoch bump + read-after-write races; multi-node chaos (node crash + write spike); staged canary on low-traffic shard
Sam: canary gating: 0.5% traffic, threshold <1% stale reads in 1s window, rollback if >5 errors or sustained latency/poly increase
ops-bot: scheduled canary: cluster=canary-3 window=2h start=2026-04-02T03:00Z
Maria: how to expose to Dedicated/Private installs? config toggle + runtime console gate and kill-switch in SDK
Alex: eviction interactions: when token exists, eviction should prefer non-shepherd slabs. reclaim shepherded slices only after grace expiration. must enforce bound to avoid leak
Kevin: add eviction_credit per token; eviction scheduler honors credit budgets -> enforces fairness and tenant isolation. credits can be tied to SLA tier
Sam: credits + fairshare sounds right. also helps with multi-tenant hotkey storms
Maria: doc & ops checklist: migration steps from soft-pin; telemetry dashboards; rollback playbook; canary checklist; KB for SRE on token telemetry interpretation
Alex: I'll draft an RFC with token lifecycle diagram (allocate -> refresh -> epoch-mismatch -> invalidate -> expire) and a tiny reference impl in the prefix layer
Kevin: include explicit invariants: "reads must reflect writes within tombstone-visibility bound" and "no silent demote that violates ordering" plus enumerated failure modes
Sam: I'll own the chaos tests and pair on the canary harness
Maria: tagging release:eng-runtime. add a short spike to measure token memory perf and GC impact
Alex: thanks. will post RFC link when ready. cc @Sam @Kevin @Maria :thumbsup:
Maria: :thumbsup:
Sam: happy to help on tests
Kevin: will write invariants tomorrow
